Kyle —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a lightweight Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused exclusively on the concurrency pilot and acceptance criteria. High level:

- Goal: Validate steady-state throughput at 300 concurrent sessions with P95 latency < 220ms and TTFT < 1200ms for 2k token responses; characterize burst behavior up to 2k concurrent requests.
- What we'll run: (a) steady-state 30m runs at target concurrency, (b) short bursts (3x target) for 2–5 minutes to observe queueing/latency spikes, (c) controlled backpressure tests with client-side rate limit ramps.
- Deliverables: CSV of per-request latencies, TTFT breakdown, KV cache hit curves; post-run recommendations (batching, quantization, rate-limit knobs).

Proposed schedule:
- Week 1 (next week): finalize eval harness + access (you give test account);
- Week 2: run steady-state + burst tests;
- Week 3: analysis and final report;
- Close: agreement signature and pilot conversion by end of week 3 if acceptance criteria met.

Attached: redwood-map-draft-v2.pdf (MAP + test plan).

Can you confirm the test account we discussed and whether the team prefers the 10/29 or 10/30 slot for the steady-state run?

Subject: Re: Concurrency pilot: schedule, benchmarks, and close timeline — evaluation plan details

Kyle / team —

Thanks — I pulled together a concise evaluation plan to answer your two questions and lock down test config. Key points below (attached: eval-harness-config.yaml + quick-run checklist):

Test types and how we generate them:
- New-session bursts: spawn independent sessions (cold KV) to surface any model init or KV fill costs. Bursts are run at 3x nominal concurrency for 3 minutes with a 1-minute ramp-up.
- Token-pressure bursts: send more tokens-per-second on a fixed set of active sessions to stress decoder throughput and batching.
- Steady-state: maintain N concurrent active sessions for 30 minutes; measure per-request P50/P95/P99 latency distribution, TTFT (first-token), token-cost per request.

Rate-limit tuning and measurement:
- We'll run three server-side rate-limit profiles (conservative, baseline, aggressive) to capture how Redwood's queueing/backpressure behaves when the headroom is low.
- Client-side throttle: we recommend a leaky-bucket emulator so you can replicate real client retry behaviour.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail gates):
- P95 < 220ms for short responses (<512 tokens) at target steady-state concurrency.
- TTFT median <1200ms for 2k token responses.
- No sustained error-rate >0.5% during steady-state.

Data we will deliver:
- concurrency-results-summary.csv (per-request rows),
- per-run dashboard links (shared Drive),
- short recommendations doc (batch sizes, KV caching knob, suggested rate-limit defaults).

Proposed run window: 2026-10-30 10:00–12:00 PDT for steady-state, 10/31 mornings for bursts (if needed). If those times work we'll spin up the harness and share credentials.

Next steps:
1) Kyle confirms test account + acceptance of the three-rate-limit profiles.
2) We run the tests and collect results.
3) Post-run review with technical write-up and recommended production knobs.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Final: concurrency pilot results snapshot + next steps (pilot close target 11/05)

Kyle / Team —

We completed the runs this morning and attached a short CSV with the raw per-request rows: concurrency-results-summary.csv. Quick highlights and recommended next steps below (detailed report is also in the shared Drive link).

Summary highlights (run: steady-state 300 sessions, 30m; bursts at ~900 concurrent for 3 minutes):
- Steady-state: P95 latency = 205ms for small responses (<=512 tokens). TTFT median for 2k token responses = 1,150ms. Error rate = 0.12%.
- Token-pressure bursts caused brief P99 spikes up to 1.8s and observable queue depth growth; however, server-side leaky-queue policy prevented sustained error growth.
- Server queue histograms (attached in the Drive) show median queue depth under steady-state ~2; during peak bursts queue depth peaked at 38 and decayed within 110s.

Recommendations:
- Default server-side rate-profile: baseline (we recommended) for production; enable a conservative fallback for early ramp to limit tail risk.
- Client guidance: implement leaky-bucket with backoff jitter; cap retry at 2 attempts for 5xx spikes.
- Immediate tactical: enable prefix KV caching for the hot prompt set we exercised — expected token-cost reduction ~8–12%.

Next steps to close:
1) FintechCo to confirm acceptance of the results & PO path (Kyle noted procurement will start PO on conditional acceptance).
2) We’ll prepare a condensed SOW addendum (3–4 pages) and DocuSign -- link attached.
3) Target signature: 2026-11-05.

Thanks for the fast collaboration — Marcus led the run and Neha did the analysis; tagging Lauren to coordinate commercial docs.

Best —
